agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: dev_a has 512 problems, with no overlap with HOLDOUT or the other DEV splits. I've split it into dev_a1 and dev_a2 of 256 each. This pass runs the frozen submission C(−1.5), unchanged, against the original on dev_a1. The C direction was built from dev_a's loops, so I'll report the result separately as in-sample. A gain consistent with the HOLDOUT +2.2 together with a cut-off drop to about 14% would be consistent with that result. A clearly negative result would be a warning sign about it.

On dev_a1, C(−1.5) scores −1.56 ± 1.99 (11 wrong→right, 15 right→wrong), even though cut-offs halve (28.1% → 14.1%). Here the freed loops mostly ended in wrong answers: wrong finished answers rose from 130 to 169. Within one standard error this is consistent with zero, and the HOLDOUT gain of +2.2 lies about 1.9 SE away, so it is a mild warning rather than a refutation.

Pooling every paired C(−1.5) measurement so far gives 121 wrong→right against 92 right→wrong over 1,994 problems: about +1.45 ± 0.75 points. That pool covers HOLDOUT 1,226, dev_b 512 and dev_a1 256. I'll run dev_a2 as planned to complete the sanity check, then report HOLDOUT and the all-sets pool side by side. If dev_a2 is also negative and the overall pool falls below about 1 SE, the evidence for C becomes weak, and I'll weigh submitting the original under the rule I set.

The notes are updated, and the frozen submission C(−1.5) (14 tensors) is unchanged. This pass completes the in-sample sanity check on dev_a2, the other 256 problems of the building set. A result near or above zero would leave the overall picture as it is, a modest gain coming from freed loops. Another clearly negative result would pull the all-sets pool toward zero, and I would reconsider the submission.

On dev_a2, C(−1.5) scores −1.17 ± 1.79 (9 wrong→right, 12 right→wrong), with cut-offs again falling, 23.8% → 14.8%. All of dev_a pooled is about −1.4 ± 1.3 (20/27 over 512). All of DEV pooled is about 0 (48/49 over 1,024). HOLDOUT remains +2.2 ± 0.95 (82/55 over 1,226). Over all 2,250 practice problems, the pool is 130 wrong→right against 104 right→wrong, about +1.2 ± 0.7.

So C reliably removes about half of all cut-offs, but whether that becomes accuracy varies between sets. The HOLDOUT gain is probably at the high end of the true effect. To see why dev_a does not gain, I'll split the flips by the original's outcome, as I did for HOLDOUT. On HOLDOUT, the originally cut problems gave 35 wrong→right against 6 right→wrong, and finished problems a wash, 47 against 49. If dev_a shows the same pattern for cut problems but a net loss among finished ones, the edit's mechanism is intact and the difference is churn noise. If even the freed loops fail to gain on dev_a, the mechanism claim is weaker.
